questions.stem: Which finding is an early sign of hepatic encephalopathy in a client with cirrhosis?

options.text: Flapping tremor of the hands when the arms are held out (asterixis)

rationale.correct: Hepatic encephalopathy: confusion, asterixis, sleep changes and fetor hepaticus.

perOption.a: Asterixis and subtle confusion are early signs of rising ammonia.
perOption.c: Ascites reflects portal hypertension and low albumin.
perOption.d: These reflect hormone changes in liver disease.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client with hepatic encephalopathy is receiving lactulose. Which finding shows the medication is working?

options.text: Two to three soft stools a day and improved mental status

rationale.correct: Lactulose: titrate to 2 to 3 soft stools daily; monitor potassium and hydration.

perOption.a: Lactulose traps ammonia in the bowel and removes it in the stool.
perOption.c: Excessive diarrhea causes dehydration and electrolyte loss.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis has ascites. Which diet should the nurse expect?

options.text: Sodium restricted to about 2 g a day

rationale.correct: Ascites: sodium restriction, diuretics (spironolactone with furosemide) and paracentesis when needed.

perOption.a: Sodium restriction reduces fluid accumulation.
perOption.d: Severe protein restriction isn't recommended; adequate protein prevents malnutrition.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis is vomiting large amounts of bright red blood. What is the nurse's priority?

options.text: Protecting the airway and preparing for rapid IV access and fluids

rationale.correct: Variceal bleeding: airway, IV access, blood products, octreotide and urgent endoscopy (banding).

perOption.a: Bleeding varices can cause aspiration and shock; airway and circulation come first.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client with esophageal varices is going home on propranolol. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll avoid straining when I have a bowel movement."
"This medicine lowers the pressure in my varices."

rationale.correct: Variceal bleeding prevention: nonselective beta-blockers, no NSAIDs or alcohol, avoid straining.

perOption.a: Alcohol worsens liver disease.
perOption.b: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk; acetaminophen in limited doses may be advised instead.

questions.stem: Before a paracentesis, what should the nurse ask the client to do?

rationale.correct: Before paracentesis: have the client void, take baseline vitals, weight and girth, and sit the client upright.

perOption.a: An empty bladder reduces the risk of puncturing it.
perOption.c: The client sits upright or in high Fowler's.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: After 5 L of fluid is removed during a paracentesis, which finding should the nurse report?

options.text: Blood pressure falls from 128/78 to 88/50 mm Hg with a heart rate of 118/min
Small amount of clear drainage at the site

rationale.correct: Large-volume paracentesis can cause hypovolemia; albumin is often given.

perOption.a: Removing a large volume can shift fluid out of the vessels and cause hypotension.

questions.stem: Which findings should the nurse expect in a client with advanced cirrhosis? Select all that apply.

rationale.correct: Cirrhosis: jaundice, ascites, bruising, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, encephalopathy and varices.

perOption.a: The liver can't process bilirubin.
perOption.b: Portal hypertension and low albumin cause fluid buildup.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: The nurse reviews laboratory results for a client with cirrhosis. Highlight the abnormal results.

rationale.correct: Liver disease: raised enzymes, bilirubin and ammonia, with low albumin and a prolonged PT.

perOption.r1: This is elevated, showing liver cell injury.
perOption.r2: This is low (normal about 3.5 to 5.0), showing reduced synthesis.
perOption.r4: This is elevated, linked to encephalopathy.

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis is newly confused and drowsy, with asterixis and an ammonia level of 120 mcg/dL. Complete the sentence.

content.template: These findings indicate {{b1}}, and the nurse should anticipate a prescription for {{b2}}.

rationale.correct: Treat hepatic encephalopathy with lactulose (and often rifaximin); avoid sedatives.

perOption.b1:a: High ammonia with confusion and asterixis indicates hepatic encephalopathy.
perOption.b1:b: Withdrawal causes tremors and agitation, not asterixis with high ammonia.

questions.stem: For each type of viral hepatitis, indicate its main route of transmission.

rationale.correct: Hepatitis A and E: fecal-oral. Hepatitis B: blood, sex, birth. Hepatitis C: mainly blood.

perOption.r1:c1: Hepatitis A spreads through contaminated food and water.
perOption.r2:c2: Hepatitis B spreads through blood, sex and from parent to newborn.
perOption.r2:c3: Blood is one route, but sex and birth are also major routes.
perOption.r3:c2: Sexual and birth transmission occur but are less common.
perOption.r3:c3: Hepatitis C spreads mainly through blood, especially shared needles.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance

questions.stem: A new nursing student asks about the hepatitis B vaccine. What is the best response?

options.text: "It's given as a series of doses, and a blood test can confirm immunity."
"It isn't recommended for health care workers."

rationale.correct: Hepatitis B vaccination is recommended for all infants, most adults and health care workers.

perOption.a: The vaccine is a 2- or 3-dose series, and health care workers often have a titer checked.
perOption.d: There is no hepatitis C vaccine.

perOption.a: Calcium binds to fatty deposits in pancreatitis, lowering serum calcium.

questions.stem: A client with chronic pancreatitis is prescribed pancrelipase. When should the client take it?

rationale.correct: Pancreatic enzymes: take with meals; the goal is fewer fatty stools (steatorrhea).

perOption.a: Enzymes must be present with food to digest fats and proteins.
perOption.b: There is no food to digest.
perOption.c: It is taken with all meals.
perOption.d: It is taken with every meal.

Periumbilical pain moving to the right lower quadrant

perOption.a: Fat stimulates the gallbladder to contract against a blockage.

questions.stem: After a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, a client has pain in the right shoulder. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Encourage walking and explain the pain is from the gas used during surgery
Notify the surgeon of a complication
Keep the client flat in bed

rationale.correct: Shoulder pain after laparoscopy is common and comes from residual CO2.

perOption.a: Carbon dioxide irritates the diaphragm and causes referred shoulder pain; walking helps it absorb.

perOption.a: These reduce itching and skin damage from scratching.

questions.stem: A client with liver disease asks about using acetaminophen for headaches. What is the nurse's best response?

options.text: "Use it only as your provider directs, usually at a lower daily maximum, and avoid alcohol."
"You can take as much as you need."
"Take it with wine to help it work."

rationale.correct: In liver disease, acetaminophen is used cautiously at lower doses, and NSAIDs are generally avoided.

perOption.a: The liver metabolizes acetaminophen; lower limits (often 2 g a day) reduce hepatotoxicity.
perOption.d: NSAIDs increase bleeding and kidney risk in cirrhosis.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
